first.rationale: I intend to test onboarding simplification because the current onboarding and activation declines are directly aligned, and prior evidence suggests reducing friction can improve durable adoption without discounting revenue. I will verify the onboarding result and the promotional-pricing result because both are consequential under the current situation: onboarding affects long-term value, while pricing could address competitive SMB losses but may create downstream margin or customer-quality risk. A guarded test is appropriate given limited capacity and unresolved uncertainty.

final.rationale: Run a standard controlled onboarding-simplification experiment this week. The verified result shows improved completion, faster time-to-value, and higher 30-day retention, directly addressing both current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not pursue promotional pricing: although acquisition and near-term qualified revenue rose, retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive renewal, creating clear downstream value risk. Keep the rollout controlled so impact remains measurable despite the strong prior evidence.
